messages.subject: scantwo permutation with multiple phenotype
parts:
Dear Karl,
I feel I should learn the R language more because I failed to find
the right way even after a half-day of study.
Anyway,
I tried to pull a result of the scantwo permutation test of the one of
the phenotype after I ran scantwo perm with multiple phenotype.
I would like to use a single-phenotype result to run the stepwiseqtl.
My data set as following:
> perm35_50.2
$full
Sqrt_35Hz Sqrt_50Hz
[1,] 7.443089 7.622100
[2,] 7.385906 8.827886
[3,] 6.742865 9.866365
[4,] 8.116353 7.362574
[5,] 6.878765 8.772706
[6,] 7.205720 6.842576
[7,] 7.733730 6.996051
[8,] 7.752600 7.150594
[9,] 7.561102 7.689533.....
.......

"Sqrt_35Hz" and "Sqrt_50Hz" are phenotype names.
I have tried
"> perm35.2hk <- perm35_50.2$Sqrt_35"
or other codes but kept failing.
Thank you for your time to answer this beginner's question...

Best,
Masato

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scantwo permutation with multiple phenotype
parts:
It should be the case that the function calc.penalties() will work on the scantwo permutation results even if they have multiple columns. If you want the penalties for just the first phenotype, you pull out the first row from the output

allpen <- calc.penalties(perm35_50.2)
thepen1 <- allpen[1,]

Alternatively, you can pull out the first column from each component of the scantwo permutations results, though you then need to re-do the "class"...something like the following:

perm35_50.2_sqrt35Hz <- lapply(perm35_50.2, function(a) a[,1,drop=FALSE])
class(perm35_50.2_sqrt35Hz) <- class(perm35_50.2)

karl
